issues: Nothing to veto. The diff changes one hyperparameter, MATRIX_LR (the Muon learning rate), from 0.04 to 0.05. It does not touch the val_bpb measurement, the data, the seed lines, the prepare.py import or the evaluation call.
No bugs found. 0.05 is a sensible Muon learning rate and does not affect memory use or run time.
The numbers are consistent. The candidate scored 1.1135 against the incumbent mean of 1.1145, a gain of 0.0010. A positive z fits this, since lower val_bpb is better.

z could not be recomputed exactly because the incumbent's spread across its 16 runs (standard deviation) was not provided. A z of 0.178 implies a spread of about 0.0056 per run, so a gain of 0.0010 is well within run-to-run noise. The provisional reject decision is reasonable. There is only one candidate run, so a replicate would be needed to resolve a gain this small.
